shouldFix.title: Decision 2's eligibility basis describes the recorded artifact as having candidate-owned classes, a structure preview-analyze-contract.v2 does not have
shouldFix.finding: Decision 2 reads: 'NT-1..NT-8 are specified-classes-not-executed and most are candidate-owned with no exact DR-G obligation, so Eligibility gates 2 and 3 are not established.' The first conjunct is accurate — v2's negativeTests.status is exactly 'specified-classes-not-executed'. The second is not. Measured in v2's own bytes, its eight classes carry only name, input and pass; there is no owner field and no existingGate field on any of them, 'this-candidate' occurs zero times and 'existingGate' occurs zero times. So no class is stated to be candidate-owned, and 'most' quantifies over a property the artifact does not assign. The phrasing is imported from the sibling DR-117 chain, where preview-product-boundary-successor.v5 does carry explicit owner and existingGate fields — and where I verified this identical sentence at D-137 turn 2 and found it accurate, because nine of that artifact's fourteen classes really are owner=this-candidate. Applying the same measurement here gives the opposite answer. The defect is confined to the basis: the conclusion is correct on either reading, since D-056's gate 3 requires the remainder to be already named at a condition-4 / DR-G* obligation with an owner and none of NT-1..NT-8 is so named, while gate 2 excludes the harness authoring those classes still require. Note also that if 'candidate-owned' were read loosely as 'owned by this candidate because no one else is named', it would be true of all eight rather than most, so 'most' mis-describes under that reading too.
shouldFix.whyNotMustFix: The operative conclusion — that recording v2 does not make DR-131 D-056-eligible in kind and that a later SATISFIED cycle must first close and independently review the owner, gate and harness design — is correct and is the most valuable sentence in the entry. Nothing else in the recording depends on the inaccurate half, and no authority is expanded by it.
shouldFix.repair: Replace the second conjunct with what is measurable in v2: no DR-G obligation names any of NT-1..NT-8 and no owner is assigned to them, so Eligibility gates 2 and 3 are not established. Keep the rest of Decision 2 exactly as drafted. If the intent was to carry the DR-117 entry's phrasing forward for consistency, say instead that this artifact assigns no class owners at all, which is a stronger statement of the same gap.

coordinatorSummary: OBJECT at 0 MUST-FIX and 1 SHOULD-FIX, with 1 advisory. Fourteen attacks run, one landed. Before the substance: the dispatch and the review prompt disagree about the subject's digest. The dispatch expects 315aa352…, the review prompt expects 46993d47…, and the live subject is 46993d47… at mode 0444. I proceeded rather than OBJECTing for motion, because the dispatch itself directs me to follow the review prompt, whose pin matches, and because the subject's mtime of 20:05:15 precedes both control files at 20:05:24 — it predates the instruments that pin it and cannot have moved since dispatch. That is a defect in the dispatch apparatus rather than in the draft, so it is recorded in custody and raised as an advisory. On the substance, the entry is strong. All eight measured-inputs rows reproduce, v2 is a genuine dual ACCEPT at 0/0, and both advisory identifiers are accurate — including Codex's reuse of its v1 identifier DR131V1-ADV-1 at v2, which I confirmed in its own bytes rather than assuming a transcription slip. The entry adopts both improvements the preceding cycles produced without being asked: Decision 6 carries D-136's owed-MF-6 form for the 'no contract exists' clause that goes stale on adoption, and Decision 2 carries D-137's statement of why the recording does not advance the row. What blocks is one clause inside that second adoption. Decision 2 says NT-1..NT-8 'are specified-classes-not-executed and most are candidate-owned with no exact DR-G obligation'. The first half is exact. The second is not: preview-analyze-contract.v2's eight classes carry only name, input and pass, with zero occurrences of 'this-candidate' or 'existingGate', so no class is stated to be candidate-owned and 'most' quantifies over a property the artifact does not assign. The phrasing is imported from the DR-117 chain, where I verified the identical sentence at D-137 turn 2 and found it accurate because that artifact really does carry owner fields. The conclusion survives on either reading, since gate 3 needs a named condition-4 obligation with an owner and none of the eight has one; only the basis needs restating to what is measurable here.
